purpose: Assess a freely readable fish-composition study in the Ibulao-Magat connected system while keeping its Ifugao landing-center data separate from Region II site records.

source.title: Fish Species Composition and Distribution from 2015 to 2019 in the Ibulao River, Ifugao, Cordillera, Philippines
source.citation: Tauli, M. P., Garcia, M. P. C., Podeque, J. R. P., Signey, L. L., Sarmiento, K., & Santos, M. D. (2022). Fish Species Composition and Distribution from 2015 to 2019 in the Ibulao River, Ifugao, Cordillera, Philippines. The Philippine Journal of Fisheries, 29(1), 90-95. https://doi.org/10.31398/tpjf/29.1.2020C0016

scopeAndMethods.reportedStudyPeriod: 2015-2019; article says January through December, with no 2019 monitoring in Kiangan
reportedLandingCenters: Lagawe; the abstract spells this as Lagave
scopeAndMethods.sampleFrame: Fish samples were taken from landed catches at the three study landing centers, using nets, traps and electrofishing; samples were preserved in 95% ethanol and sent to the NFRDI Genetic Fingerprinting Laboratory for identification.
reportedIdentificationMethods: DNA fingerprinting at the NFRDI Genetic Fingerprinting Laboratory
scopeAndMethods.waterbodyContext: The paper describes the Ibulao River as an Ifugao river that drains to Magat Dam and states that the river system covers parts of Ifugao and Isabela.
scopeAndMethods.localityConfidence: Waterbody and broad municipality/landing-center context are reported, but no fish-level capture coordinates, station-to-catch crosswalk, specimen catalog numbers, sequence accessions, or released voucher table were located. The paper does not place its three landing centers in Isabela. Treat this as an adjacent CAR source connected to the Magat system, not a Region II-local occurrence dataset.

sourceQualityAndRightsFlags: The abstract says 18 fish species in 11 families; the body says 18 finfishes in 12 families. Preserve both source statements pending author clarification.
Table 1 prints Caracius caracius, while Table 3 prints Carassius carassius. Do not silently correct or merge these labels before taxonomic review.

Four table entries are BFARCAR laboratory labels rather than resolved species names; Nomorhamphus sp. is genus-level. No individual specimen identifiers or DNA sequence accessions are published in the reviewed paper.
Table 2 lists Kiangan, Lagawe, and Ifugao, while the abstract and methods name Lamut, Kiangan, and Lagawe. This unresolved landing-center discrepancy limits locality-specific use.
Table 1's status labels (native, introduced, endemic, and further identification) are source-reported and have not been independently checked here.

The article states CC BY-NC 4.0. This permits attribution-based noncommercial sharing under its terms, not commercial reuse. Bangwit's future commercial status is unresolved, so no app or public species/occurrence projection is approved.
Table 3 reports no Kiangan monitoring in 2019 due to reduced enumerator staffing; this is a sampling gap, not a zero-catch or species-absence observation.

disposition.researchUse: Useful open research lead for the adjacent Ibulao-Magat freshwater system; retain the verbatim source labels and explicit municipality/table conflicts.

nextAction: Find and review fully accessible, site-resolved fish or voucher studies from Isabela and other Region II watersheds; keep upstream Ifugao findings separated unless a specific source links a sample to a Region II locality.
